questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates practical DevOps security skills by testing your ability to implement automated security gates that prevent secret leakage and ensure deployment consistency, directly connecting code hygiene to CI/CD workflows.

## Key Concepts
- Secret scanning integration in CI pipelines
- Baseline management for handling false positives
- Comprehensive coverage of manifests and Helm values
- Local development vs CI environment verification
- Image tag approval and enforcement workflows
- Automated security gates in pull request processes

## Code Example

### GitHub Actions CI Workflow
```yaml
# .github/workflows/security-scan.yml
name: Secret Scan & Image Validation
on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - '**/*.yaml'
      - '**/*.yml'
      - '**/values.yaml'
      - '**/Chart.yaml'

jobs:
  security-scan:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Install detect-secrets
        run: pip install detect-secrets

      - name: Scan for secrets
        run: |
          # Initialize baseline if it doesn't exist
          if [ ! -f .secrets.baseline ]; then
            detect-secrets scan --baseline .secrets.baseline
          fi
          
          # Run scan and fail if new secrets detected
          detect-secrets scan --baseline .secrets.baseline --all-files
          
          # Check for any high-entropy results
          if detect-secrets audit --report .secrets.baseline | grep -q "High Entropy"; then
            echo "❌ Secrets detected! Please review and remove before merging."
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Validate image tags
        run: |
          # Define approved tags (in production, store this securely)
          APPROVED_TAGS="v1.2.0,v1.2.1,latest"
          
          # Extract image tags from manifests
          grep -r "image:" . --include="*.yaml" --include="*.yml" | \
            sed 's/.*:\s*//' | sed 's/"//g' | sed 's/.*://' | \
            sort -u > /tmp/current_tags.txt
          
          # Validate each tag
          while IFS= read -r tag; do
            if [[ "$APPROVED_TAGS" != *"$tag"* ]]; then
              echo "❌ Image tag '$tag' is not in approved list: $APPROVED_TAGS"
              exit 1
            fi
          done < /tmp/current_tags.txt
          
          echo "✅ All image tags are approved"

      - name: Comment on PR (if failed)
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          script: |
            github.rest.issues.createComment({
              issue_number: context.issue.number,
              owner: context.repo.owner,
              repo: context.repo.repo,
              body: '🚨 **Security Scan Failed**\n\nThis PR contains either hardcoded secrets or unapproved image tags. Please review the failed job and fix the issues before merging.'
            })
```

### Example Manifest That Would Fail
```yaml
# deployment-with-secrets.yaml (THIS WOULD FAIL THE SCAN)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: webapp
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: webapp
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: webapp
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: webapp
        # ❌ Unapproved image tag - will fail validation
        image: myregistry/webapp:v1.3.0-beta
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8080
        env:
        # ❌ Hardcoded secret - will fail scanning
        - name: DATABASE_PASSWORD
          value: "super-secret-password-12345"
        - name: API_KEY
          value: "AKIA1234567890ABCDEFGHI"
        # ❌ Another high-entropy string
        - name: JWT_SECRET
          value: "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJzdWIiOiIxMjM0NTY3ODkwIiwibmFtZSI6IkpvaG4gRG9lIiwiaWF0IjoxNTE2MjM5MDIyfQ"
```

### Configuration Files

#### detect-secrets Configuration
```yaml
# .detect-secrets.yml
version: "0.14"
plugins:
  - name: ArtifactoryDetector
    path: detect_secrets.plugins.artifactory
  - name: AWSKeyDetector
    path: detect_secrets.plugins.aws
  - name: Base64HighEntropyString
    path: detect_secrets.plugins.high_entropy_strings
    baseline:
      charset: "base64"
      min_entropy: 4.5  # Adjust for false positives
  - name: HexHighEntropyString
    path: detect_secrets.plugins.high_entropy_strings
    baseline:
      charset: "hex"
      min_entropy: 3.0
  - name: KeywordDetector
    path: detect_secrets.plugins.keyword
    keyword_exclude: "passkey,password"  # Add safe keywords
  - name: PrivateKeyDetector
    path: detect_secrets.plugins.private_key
  - name: SlackTokenDetector
    path: detect_secrets.plugins.slack

filters:
  - detect_secrets.filters.common.is_likely_id_string
  - detect_secrets.filters.heuristic.is_indented_comment
  - detect_secrets.filters.heuristic.is_potential_uuid
  - detect_secrets.filters.heuristic.is_sequential_string

# Paths to exclude from scanning
exclude_files:
  - "tests/.*\.mock\.yaml$"
  - "docs/.*\.md$"
```

#### Pre-commit Hook Configuration
```yaml
# .pre-commit-config.yaml
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/Yelp/detect-secrets
    rev: v1.4.0
    hooks:
      - id: detect-secrets
        args: ['--baseline', '.secrets.baseline']
  
  - repo: local
    hooks:
      - id: validate-image-tags
        name: Validate image tags
        entry: bash -c '
          APPROVED_TAGS="v1.2.0,v1.2.1,latest" &&
          grep -r "image:" . --include="*.yaml" --include="*.yml" |
          sed "s/.*:\s*//" | sed "s/\"//g" | sed "s/.*://" |
          sort -u | while read tag; do
            if [[ "$APPROVED_TAGS" != *"$tag"* ]]; then
              echo "❌ Image tag \"$tag\" is not approved"
              exit 1
            fi
          done'
        language: system
        files: \.(yaml|yml)$
```

## Local Verification Steps

### 1. Install Dependencies
```bash
# Install detect-secrets
pip install detect-secrets

# Install pre-commit hooks
pip install pre-commit
pre-commit install
```

### 2. Initial Setup
```bash
# Create initial baseline
find . -name "*.yaml" -o -name "*.yml" | xargs detect-secrets scan > .secrets.baseline

# Review and audit the baseline
detect-secrets audit .secrets.baseline
```

### 3. Test the Workflow
```bash
# Test with a problematic file (should fail)
cat > test-bad.yaml << EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: test-secret
data:
  password: c3VwZXItc2VjcmV0LXBhc3N3b3JkLTEyMzQ1  # base64 encoded secret
EOF

# Run the scan (should fail)
detect-secrets scan --baseline .secrets.baseline test-bad.yaml

# Clean up
rm test-bad.yaml
```

### 4. Test Image Tag Validation
```bash
# Create deployment with unapproved tag
cat > test-deployment.yaml << EOF
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: test
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: myapp:v2.0.0  # Not in approved list
EOF

# This should fail the image tag validation
grep -r "image:" . --include="*.yaml" | sed 's/.*:\s*//' | sed 's/"//g' | sed 's/.*://'

rm test-deployment.yaml
```

## How to Verify in CI

1. **Push a test PR** with problematic files to your fork
2. **Check GitHub Actions** tab to see the security scan job
3. **Verify the job fails** when secrets or unapproved tags are detected
4. **Fix the issues** and push again to confirm the job passes
5. **Review PR comments** for automated notifications when scans fail

## Best Practices

- Store approved image tags in a config file or secret management system
- Use semantic versioning for image tags
- Implement secret management (Kubernetes Secrets, Vault, etc.)
- Regularly update the baseline after auditing
- Enable dependency scanning for container images
- Use image signing and verification for production deployments

## Why This Is Asked

Tests understanding of Helm templating and basic policy checks in CI for secure defaults, plus ability to craft a simple gate that a junior engineer can implement.

## Key Concepts

- Helm templating and values.yaml
- YAML validation with yq
- Kubernetes securityContext basics
- Image tag policy and registry scoping
- CI gate design and test manifests

## Code Example

```yaml
# .github/workflows/helm-gate.yml
name: Helm gate
on: push
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - uses: azure/setup-helm@v1
      - name: Render charts
        run: helm template mychart charts/mychart > /tmp/rendered.yaml
      - name: Validate images
        run: |
          if ! yq e '.items[].spec.template.spec.containers[].image' /tmp/rendered.yaml | grep -q registry.example.com/secure/; then echo image origin invalid; exit 1; fi
```

```yaml
# failing Deployment manifest
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: myservice
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: app
          image: registry.example.com/secure/myservice:latest
          # missing securityContext and resources
```

```yaml
# passing Deployment manifest
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: myservice
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: app
          image: registry.example.com/secure/myservice:v1.2.3
```

## Why This Is Asked
This question tests the ability to enforce end-to-end data provenance and reproducibility across hybrid multi-tenant environments, combining image signing, SBOM management, and centralized provenance tracking to guard against tampered or non-reproducible artifacts.

## Key Concepts
- End-to-end data provenance across on-prem and cloud environments
- Reproducible builds with digests tied to provenance records
- Attestation formats (SBOM via CycloneDX) and cryptographic signing (Sigstore/cosign)
- Policy-as-code (Kyverno/OPA) for admission control
- CI/CD pipeline integration (GitHub Actions) and runtime verification

## Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal GitHub Actions workflow for ML model artifact pipeline
name: Model Artifact Pipeline

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths: ['models/**']

jobs:
  build-and-sign:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      
      - name: Build model image
        run: |
          docker build -t model-api:${GITHUB_SHA} ./models/
      
      - name: Generate SBOM
        run: |
          syft model-api:${GITHUB_SHA} -o cyclonedx-json > model.sbom.json
      
      - name: Sign with cosign
        run: |
          cosign sign --key cosign.key model-api:${GITHUB_SHA}
      
      - name: Attach SBOM attestation
        run: |
          cosign attest --type cyclonedx --key cosign.key \
            --predicate model.sbom.json model-api:${GITHUB_SHA}
      
      - name: Upload provenance
        run: |
          curl -X POST $PROVENANCE_STORE_URL/attestations \
            -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
            -d '{"digest":"'$GITHUB_SHA'","sbom":"model.sbom.json","signature":"cosign"}'
```

```yaml
# Kyverno policy for admission control
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: ml-model-admission
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Enforce
  rules:
    - name: verify-cosign-signature
      match:
        resources:
          kinds:
            - Pod
      validate:
        message: "Model image must be cosign-signed"
        pattern:
          spec:
            containers:
              - image: "!*"
    - name: verify-sbom-attestation
      match:
        resources:
          kinds:
            - Pod
      validate:
        message: "SBOM attestation required"
        pattern:
          spec:
            containers:
              - image: "!*"
```

## Verification Steps

**Local Verification:**
```bash
# Verify cosign signature
cosign verify --key cosign.pub model-api:latest

# Verify SBOM attestation
cosign attestation verify --type cyclonedx model-api:latest

# Check reproducibility digest
reproctl verify --provenance $PROVENANCE_STORE_URL
```

**CI Verification:**
```yaml
verify-attestations:
  needs: build-and-sign
  runs-on: ubuntu-latest
  steps:
    - name: Verify all attestations
      run: |
        cosign verify --key cosign.pub model-api:${GITHUB_SHA}
        cosign attestation verify --type cyclonedx model-api:${GITHUB_SHA}
```

## Why This Is Asked
- Tests understanding of namespace-scoped network policies and the allow-by-default model.
- Checks ability to craft precise egress rules and test scenarios.
- Evaluates how to verify traffic patterns in a live cluster.

## Key Concepts
- Kubernetes NetworkPolicy basics, podSelector, egress rules
- Protocols: TCP/UDP, DNS traffic behavior
- Verification: controlled test pods and curl/dig tests

## Code Example
```yaml
# Deny-all egress by default is achieved by allowing only specific egress in a policy
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-web-egress
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: web
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - podSelector: {}
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.0.0.25/32
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.0.0.0/16
    ports:
    - protocol: UDP
      port: 53
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 53
```

- How would you validate that the policy is enforced in a multi-tenant environment?

## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates practical dependency security skills in a real monorepo environment containing both JavaScript and Python services, along with understanding of license compliance policies.

- Integrating npm audit and pip-audit into CI pipelines
- Lightweight license allowlist enforcement

## Code Example

```yaml
# .github/workflows/dependency-security.yml
name: Dependency Security Gate
on: [pull_request]

jobs:
  security-gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      
      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '20'
      
      - name: Setup Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.11'
      
      - name: Install Node dependencies
        run: npm ci
      
      - name: Install Python dependencies
        run: pip install -r requirements.txt
      
      - name: Run npm audit
        run: npm audit --audit-level=high
      
      - name: Run pip-audit
        run: pip-audit -r requirements.txt
      
      - name: Check licenses
        run: |
          npx license-checker --json > licenses.json
          # Script checks licenses against allowlist
```

## Code Example

```yaml
# Kyverno policy skeleton
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-digest-private-registry
spec:
  validationFailureAction: enforce
  rules:
  - name: digest-required
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Deployment", "DaemonSet", "StatefulSet"]
    validate:
      message: "Images must reference a digest and use private registry with imagePullSecrets."
      pattern:
        spec.template.spec.containers[].image: '*@sha256:*'
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design a reject-by-default policy for hostPath usage, a common attack surface, and to describe how to maintain a dynamic allowlist in production.

## Key Concepts
- Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate and Constraint
- hostPath volumes and host filesystem access risk
- dynamic allowlist via a ConfigMap and a small controller to sync data
- CI validation (dry-run, gatekeeper admissions) and runtime validation

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: HostPathPolicy
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: HostPathConstraint
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |
      package hostpathpolicy
      violation[{"msg": msg}] {
        input.review.kind.kind == "Pod"
        some i in input.review.object.spec.volumes
        input.review.object.spec.volumes[i].hostPath
        not data.hostpath_allowlist.namespaces[_]
        msg := "hostPath volumes are forbidden unless in allowlist"
      }
```

```yaml
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: HostPathConstraint
metadata:
  name: hostpath-deny
spec:
  match:
    kinds:
    - apiGroups: ["v1"]
      kinds: ["Pod"]
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests understanding of namespace isolation and basic egress filtering using NetworkPolicy. It checks hands-on ability to craft minimal, enforceable rules and verify them.

## Key Concepts
- Kubernetes NetworkPolicy basics
- Namespace-scoped isolation
- Egress rules and default deny
- Basic verification via kubectl and logs

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: test-egress-isolate
  namespace: test
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.1.2.3/32
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector: {}
      podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: dns
    ports:
    - protocol: UDP
      port: 53
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 0.0.0.0/0
        except:
        - 255.255.255.255/32
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 53
```

```yaml
# Compliant Pod in test namespace
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: compliant-pod
  namespace: test
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox
    command: ["sh", "-c", "sleep 300"]
```

```yaml
# Noncompliant Pod in test namespace (tries to access prod)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: noncompliant-pod
  namespace: test
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox
    command: ["sh", "-c", "wget http://prod.svc.cluster.local || true"]
```

```yaml
# DNS test Pod (for compliance with DNS allow rule)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: dns-test
  namespace: test
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox
    command: ["sh", "-c", "nslookup kubernetes.default.svc.cluster.local"]
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Fintech workloads handling sensitive financial data demand strict data-protection posture. This question validates your understanding of end-to-end security enforcement—from CI gates that catch misconfigurations before deployment to runtime policies that protect running workloads.

## Key Concepts
- CI gate for manifest validation at pull request stage
- Resource requests/limits for resource governance
- readOnlyRootFilesystem for filesystem security
- TLS secret mounting with tls-cert-<app> naming convention
- Runtime policy enforcement via Kyverno or OPA
- Verification strategies for both CI and cluster runtime

## Code Example
```yaml
# Kyverno ClusterPolicy
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-secure-deploy
spec:
  rules:
  - name: enforce-resources-readonly
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Deployment
        - Pod
    validate:
      message: "Deployment must set resources.limits, resources.requests, and readOnlyRootFilesystem: true"
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              securityContext:
                readOnlyRootFilesystem: "true"
              containers:
              - resources:
                  limits:
                    memory: "?*"
                    cpu: "?*"
                  requests:
                    memory: "?*"
                    cpu: "?*"
  - name: enforce-tls-secret-mount
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Pod
    validate:
      message: "TLS secret must be mounted at /etc/tls from Secret tls-cert-<app>"
      pattern:
        spec:
          volumes:
          - secret:
              secretName: tls-cert-?*
              items:
              - key: tls.crt
                path: etc/tls/tls.crt
```

## Sample Compliant Manifest
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: tls-cert-payment-service
type: kubernetes.io/tls
data:
  tls.crt: <base64-cert>
  tls.key: <base64-key>
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: payment-service
spec:
  replicas: 2
  template:
    spec:
      securityContext:
        readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: payment-service:latest
        resources:
          limits:
            memory: "512Mi"
            cpu: "500m"
          requests:
            memory: "256Mi"
            cpu: "250m"
        volumeMounts:
        - name: tls-certs
          mountPath: /etc/tls
          readOnly: true
      volumes:
      - name: tls-certs
        secret:
          secretName: tls-cert-payment-service
```

## Sample Non-Compliant Manifest
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: insecure-service
spec:
  replicas: 2
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: insecure-service:latest
        # Missing: resources.limits/requests
        # Missing: readOnlyRootFilesystem
        # Missing: TLS secret mount
```

## GitHub Actions CI Gate
```yaml
name: Security Gate
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  security-check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    - name: Install kubeval
      run: |4
        curl -L -o kubeval https://github.com/instrumenta/kubeval/releases/latest/download/kubeval-linux-amd64.tar.gz
        tar xf kubeval-linux-amd64.tar.gz
        sudo mv kubeval /usr/local/bin
    - name: Validate manifests
      run: |
        for f in k8s/*.yaml; do
          kubeval --strict --additional-schema-locations=https://kubernetesjsonschema.dev $f || exit 1
        done
    - name: Check resource limits
      run: |
        yq -e '.spec.template.spec.containers[].resources.limits' k8s/*.yaml || exit 1
    - name: Check readOnlyRootFilesystem
      run: |
        yq -e '.spec.template.spec.securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem == true' k8s/*.yaml || exit 1
    - name: Check TLS secret mounting
      run: |
        yq -e '.spec.template.spec.volumes[].secret.secretName | test("^tls-cert-")' k8s/*.yaml || exit 1
```

## Verification Steps

### CI Verification
1. Create a PR with the non-compliant manifest—pipeline should fail
2. Update to compliant manifest—pipeline should pass
3. Confirm all three checks (resources, readOnlyRootFilesystem, TLS) are enforced

### Runtime Verification
1. Apply Kyverno policy to test cluster
2. Attempt to deploy non-compliant manifest—deployment should be blocked
3. Verify policy logs show rejection reason
4. Apply compliant manifest—deployment should succeed

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to enforce secure secret handling across multi-cloud clusters, using policy-as-code, and integrating cert-manager with GitOps pipelines.

## Key Concepts
- Policy as code (Kyverno/OPA)
- cert-manager Certificate -> Secret flow
- ExternalSecret / SecretStore integration
- CI gating and canary verification

## Code Example
```yaml
# Kyverno policy (example)
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-inline-tls-and-enforce-secretref
spec:
  validationFailureAction: fail
  rules:
  - name: deny-inline-tls
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Deployment", "StatefulSet"]
    validate:
      message: "TLS data must come from cert-manager SecretRef; do not inline certificates"
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              volumes:
              - secret:
                  secretName: "?!*"
```

```rego
# OPA/ValidatingAdmissionPolicy (illustrative)
package kubernetes.admission

deny[{"msg":"inline certs not allowed"}] {
  input.request.kind.kind == "Deployment" or input.request.kind.kind == "StatefulSet"
  some i
  secret := input.request.object.spec.template.spec.volumes[i]
  secret.secretName != "" # ensure SecretRef used, not inline data
}
```

```yaml
# Failing manifest (inline cert example)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: tls-secret
type: kubernetes.io/tls
data:
  tls.crt: LS0tLS1CRUdJTiBDRVJUSUZJQ0FURS0tLS0t... # inline cert data
  tls.key: LS0tLS1CRUdJTiBSU0EgUFJ...
```

```yaml
# Passing manifest (SecretRef to cert-manager Secret)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      volumes:
      - name: tls
        secret:
          secretName: my-cert-manager-secret
```

```yaml
# CI validation steps (high level)
- lint manifests
- run policy gate (Kyverno/OPA) on PR
- validate that Deployment references cert-manager Secret (no inline data)
- run a quick canary test in a staging cluster
```

- How would you test this in a mono-repo with many teams?
